questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was particularly drawn to the cultural experience of living in Australia and the opportunity to study in an English-speaking environment. This combination felt both academically relevant and personally enriching.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy. Deakin University has a very informative website, almost too informative at times, which meant that most of the practical questions I had were already answered online.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any specific or structured assistance upon arrival, but general support was available if needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were several housing options, mostly shared houses or apartments where you could live with up to 10 other students.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: My apartment had a private kitchen, and there were also shared common kitchens available. However, students were required to purchase all their own cookware and utensils.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There are many international students in the housing areas, which makes it easy to meet people but not many locals. Rooms are very basic only a bed, wardrobe, desk, and chair are provided, so be prepared to buy everything else you need to make the space feel like home. Also Campus is placed pretty far from the city center, prepare to take a lot of public transport.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The process involves some back-and-forth: even after KU allocates you a spot, you still need to complete a formal application through Deakin. Fortunately, everything went smoothly. Deakin sends all required documents and forms, and the steps are clearly outlined.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The administrative staff were very friendly and ready to help with any questions throughout the process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to register for all the courses I had hoped to take.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Pay close attention to intensive courses, as these typically take place over about a week and involve very concentrated teaching. Also make sure to check whether a course is at the bachelor’s or master’s level, depending on what you need. If in doubt, contact the administration they are very helpful.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: There was a clear difference between BA and MA courses, but overall the academic level was not higher than what I have experienced at the University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Some courses had a similar structure to UCPH, while others were noticeably more interactive and engaging. Class sizes also varied significantly, which influenced the teaching style.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ADS734 GEOPOLITICS AND POLITICAL ECONOMY OF DEVELOPMENT 
AIP347 MEDIA AND POLITICS: CAMPAIGN STRATEGIES 
AIR349 DIPLOMACY AND THE UNITED NATIONS 
ALR718 PUBLIC RELATIONS, ACTIVISM AND SOCIAL CHANGE

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
AIR349 – Diplomacy and the United Nations
Highly engaging course with a unique approach: each student represents a country in a simulated UN setting.

ALR718 – Public Relations, Activism and Social Change
Taught by Thaera, who is extremely engaging and brings a dynamic and thought-provoking perspective to public relations.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Used more on public transportation as Campus was placed faraway from the city and groceries.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Less expensive to go out to eat but groceries where expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were plenty of opportunities - cultural events, sports clubs, and various social gatherings. However, not all clubs were equally easy to join when staying for only one semester, as some activities require longer-term commitment.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you live on Res (on-campus housing), there are many free weekly activities that change from week to week. They are great for meeting new people and settling into the community.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Australia offers countless beautiful places to explore, but the Great Ocean Road is an absolute must-see. It’s one of the most scenic coastal drives in the world.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The Australian culture is not very different from Danish culture - if anything, it’s more relaxed - so it was generally easy to adapt.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I lived with other international students, so I was exposed to multiple cultures beyond the Australian one. The biggest challenges were adjusting to different food habits and sleeping routines within the shared housing.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Australians are incredibly outgoing and helpful, which I really appreciated. It made everyday interactions warm and enjoyable.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Save up beforehand so you can travel and explore Australia as much as possible.
Take time to explore the wide range of courses Deakin offers - there are many unique options.
Be social from the beginning. It can be exhausting at first, but it makes a huge difference in building a network and settling in.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware of the location of the Deakin campus it is quite a distance from central Melbourne, so factor that into your expectations for commuting and city activities.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I gained both academically and personally, but the most rewarding aspect was learning to stand on my own in a new country, new culture, and new university environment. It taught me a great deal about myself.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: For me, the biggest challenge was speaking English all the time and participating actively in classes in a second language. However, it was also the aspect that taught me the most.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
